newsitem.title: GERMANY: German coalition meets to discuss budget.
newsitem.headline: German coalition meets to discuss budget.

text.p: Germany's conservative coalition met on Tuesday to discuss budget and tax plans amid continued bickering despite a call from Chancellor Helmut Kohl for an end to attacks on his Finance Minister Theo Waigel.

Leading politicians from Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU), Waigel's Bavarian Christian Social Union (CSU) and the liberal Free Democrats were to discuss Thursday's passage of the 1997 tax bill and finalising next year's budget.
Waigel has been under a barrage of criticism from the FDP after he had proposed a hike in petrol taxes to cover mounting gaps in his finance plans.

The FDP blocked the petrol tax hike by agreeing to postpone a one-point cut in the hated solidarity surcharge for a year. But it now wants the levy to be cut by two percentage points instead of one in 1998.

Juergen Moellemann, regional chief of the FDP in North Rhine-Westphalia, told German radio on Tuesday morning that deputies from his region would vote down the government's budget if the two-point cut is not assured this week.
Coalition party finance experts and parliamentary groups were also to discuss finance and tax policy in separate meetings on Tuesday.
Waigel wants to keep the budget deficit next year on target for Germany to meet the Maastricht treaty's ceiling of three percent of gross domestic product and qualify for European monetary union.
But the exact amount he will have to save will not be clear until the latest tax revenue estimates are finalised towards the end of the week.
